transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but I guess what brings me in is that I've been having a bit of trouble at work lately. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit at my age, to be honest, but I just can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. Like, I'm a computer support specialist, and I'll sit down to start tracing a client's network problem, and then... maybe ten minutes later, I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times and I still don't know what they actually say. 

I know it probably sounds like a small thing, but it's really starting to get in the way of doing a good job. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Has this kind of trouble focusing been something you've dealt with since childhood or your school years, or is this really a new change for you that started more recently?

Well, um... I guess it's not entirely new. I mean, I've always managed, you know? I did well enough to get my master's degree, so it couldn't have been too terrible. But... yeah, I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it's been there for a long time. 

My mother actually still jokes about my old report cards from grade school. She says the teachers always wrote that I was bright—which was nice of them to say!—but they'd also write that I, um... well, that I had a hard time staying in my seat, or that I'd blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking the question. And I'd lose my homework. Even when I had actually done it, which was the most frustrating part. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I was a bad kid or anything. I really tried to be good, I just... I don't know, I guess I had a lot of energy back then. Does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, anxious, or unusually worried, that might be affecting your concentration?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I feel pretty normal, mood-wise. I'm not feeling sad or down or anything like that. And I wouldn't say I'm unusually worried... well, aside from just wanting to do a good job at work and hoping I can get this sorted out, of course! 

But no, I'm generally a pretty upbeat guy. It's really just the focus thing that's been the problem. I feel perfectly fine otherwise. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way... is that what you were asking about?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic difficulty sustaining attention on tasks (e.g., rereading network logs without comprehension) causing current occupational impairment. History confirms childhood-onset symptoms including motor hyperactivity (difficulty staying seated), impulsivity (blurting answers), and inattention/disorganization (losing completed homework), as corroborated by report card history. Mood and anxiety symptoms were explicitly denied, ruling out primary mood or anxiety disorder as the cause of concentration difficulty. The combination of childhood-onset inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms persisting into adulthood with functional impairment supports a diagnosis of ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0).
